answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol enforces exponential stake burning where each identity registered by an entity scales cost as C(n)=B^n. Every agent signs its registration using a cryptographic quill, burning valuable tokens irrecoverably into an unspendable karst sink rather than a recyclable pool. This irreversible economic friction acts like an immutable lotus rooted in verifiable cost, making mass identity replication mathematically ruinous.
